opti-1: April 2010. Deep in the Gulf of Mexico, an oil well breaks open.
opti-2: Oil rises and spreads across the sea.
opti-3: Crews race out with long floating walls called booms.
opti-5: Crews pick up sticky tar, one handful at a time.
opti-7: And then, they let them go.
opti-8: So can we really clean polluted water? And does the way we do it matter?
23-02-welcome: Our film starts with a ticking clock and a giant oil spill. First, inspect some strange tubes on a beach.
23-02-lesson: Today you're a cleanup engineer. Watch a spill get cleaned up, test two tools, then follow water through a marsh that cleans it.
23-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
23-02-assign: Time to show what you found. Rate the three methods, then tell us which one you'd choose and why.
how-23-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the beach, then tap three things you notice.
how-23-02-compare: Put the pad under one tray and the net under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Try the cleanup. Then swap and try again.
how-23-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing stop: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the place shows.
how-23-02-det: Pick three cases, one at a time. Tap a clue, then pick the cleanup method. Predict whether it worked, and watch the place today appear.
how-23-02-partc: Draw a polluted lake before and after a cleanup with your best method. Label the pollution and the tool, and one living thing that is helped.
